A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Flow-of-Options work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on data-science and therapeutic-chemistry tasks, reinforcement learning, image generation, and additional appendix tasks and analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds LLM comparisons, component ablations, scaling measurements, and a retrieval-assisted option-generation example.

M1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds a demonstrated variant that supplies two retrieved research papers to the Option Generator. The core graph construction, max updates, beam traversal, consistency checking, case-based reasoning, and component prompts remain unchanged. Nested FoO is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds a small planning scenario for protein-language-model fine-tuning using retrieved papers; it reports generated options, not completed fine-tuning. Existing datasets and task variants are retained. Table 10's additional TDC columns reuse datasets already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds DeepMol to the additional-LLM comparison in Table 10, where it was absent in v1 despite appearing in the main TDC experiment. The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Main benchmark settings remain unchanged. New studies introduce Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, a CW timing sweep over n=1–3 and k=2–4 with pruning excluded, and comparisons with and without the consistency checker and adapter. These are added experimental designs, not revisions to the principal benchmark protocol.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence through component cost attribution, depth/width scaling measurements, and consistency-checker and adapter timing ablations. Appendix C broadens LLM robustness checks, while Appendix G.1 adds a retrieval case study. Existing beam-width and task-adaptation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 10 now explicitly states that results are averaged across three runs; v1's caption only specified three attempts for the failure entry. This adds run-count and aggregation disclosure without establishing an increase in runs. Principal experiments retain their three-run reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and resource-table values are unchanged after matching Tables 2 and 3 across versions. Substantial new results include GPT-3.5 outcomes on BI, BB, and PP, six-task Qwen comparisons, scaling times, component cost shares, and reported execution-time reductions of 22.8% and 93.1% in Table 11. The appendix also corrects SELA's approximate runtime from 23 to 21 minutes.

T1.justification: Section 5 adds an explicit O(k^n) complexity characterization and the argument that increasing n from 1 to 3 at k=3 multiplies possible paths ninefold. Existing graph, update, and beam-selection mathematics remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain FoO-driven solution diversity, reusable task representations, improved benchmark ranks, sub-dollar operation, and applicability beyond conventional classification and regression. The headline improvement ranges are identical; abstract edits do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of component costs and practical scaling, identifies the single-plan restriction motivating nested FoO, and discusses retrieval as a remedy for knowledge limitations. Appendix D adds a stronger human-expert-comparability interpretation of the unchanged aggregate comparison. Existing limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release in Appendix A; v2 states in the abstract that the code is open-sourced at the same repository. This changes reported availability, although the PDFs alone cannot verify repository contents. Existing component prompts, user templates, and principal hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Elnaggar et al.'s ProtTrans/ProtBERT work and Rives et al.'s ESM work for the retrieval example. Positioning against DS-Agent, SELA, Data Interpreter, and other existing approaches remains substantially unchanged; publication-metadata updates do not constitute additional research changes.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected passages are revised, terminology is refined, and appendix sections are regrouped and reordered. Scalability, future-work, and impact sections are added, but most existing methodological exposition, experimental narrative, and prompts are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout, separates several composite figures, and replaces three word-cloud displays with labeled proportion bar charts. It also adds cost and scaling figures, a component-ablation table, and an expanded Table 10. These substantially change visual presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Component ablations, scaling measurements, and broader LLM checks provide useful support missing from v1, while clearer distribution plots and reported code release improve inspectability and reproducibility information. The gain is limited: principal benchmark evidence is unchanged, the new studies are narrow, and Appendix D's stronger human-expert-comparability interpretation exceeds what the unchanged aggregate figure alone establishes.
